# The Amazing Race Dataset & AI Training Corpus

> A comprehensive tidy relational dataset and AI training corpus for the CBS reality competition television series The Amazing Race.

The Amazing Race (TAR) dataset provides structured, relational tables adhering to tidy data principles across 36 US seasons. The dataset is exported in CSV, Apache Parquet, SQLite (`tar.db`), Apache Arrow IPC, and native R (`.rds`, `.rda`) formats, alongside fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) JSONL corpora.

For complete documentation in a single prompt-ready file, see [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/main/llms-full.txt).

## Core Relational Tables

The dataset consists of 7 normalized relational tables linked by explicit foreign keys:

- [seasons](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#1-seasons): Season-level summaries including winner, runner-up, premiere/finale dates, legs count, total distance in miles/km, and destination summary. Primary key: `season`.
- [episodes](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#2-episodes): Episode-level metadata including episode title, air dates, rating, and viewership. Composite key: `(season, episode_order)`. Foreign key: `season -> seasons.season`.
- [teams](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#3-teams): Team profiles including racer names, pre-existing relationship, finish placement, legs racing average, and elimination leg. Primary key: `team_id`. Foreign key: `season -> seasons.season`.
- [contestants](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#4-contestants): Individual racer demographics, age, occupation, hometown, and biological gender. Primary key: `contestant_id`. Foreign key: `team_id -> teams.team_id`.
- [legs](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#5-legs): Leg itineraries, starting/ending locations, pit stop locations, countries visited, distance, and leg type (regular, non-elimination, keep racing, double length). Primary key: `leg_id`. Foreign key: `season -> seasons.season`.
- [leg_results](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#6-leg_results): Team placements per leg, arrival order, departure order, time deltas, yield/u-turn usage, and leg status (eliminated, saved). Composite key: `(leg_id, team_id)`. Foreign keys: `leg_id -> legs.leg_id`, `team_id -> teams.team_id`.
- [tasks](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/docs/data_dictionary.md#7-tasks): Detailed challenge records for each leg including task type (roadblock, detour, fast forward, hazard, speed bump), task description, location, and assigned racer. Foreign keys: `leg_id -> legs.leg_id`, `team_id -> teams.team_id`.

## AI Training Corpora (`data/ai/`)

- [tar_qa_finetuning.jsonl](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/data/ai/tar_qa_finetuning.jsonl): High-quality multi-turn question-answer pairs formatted for OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Covers trivia, game rules, penalties, route facts, and elimination mechanics.
- [tar_knowledge_corpus.jsonl](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/data/ai/tar_knowledge_corpus.jsonl): Structured narrative documents with metadata (`season`, `leg`, `route`) for semantic search, vector database retrieval (RAG), and embedding generation.
- [tar_benchmark_suite.jsonl](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/blob/main/data/ai/tar_benchmark_suite.jsonl): 45 curated evaluation benchmark questions with verified ground truths and rubrics covering rules comprehension, route accuracy, and trivia.

## Published Release Packages

Assets available on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/releases):

- **Tidy CSV (`tar-dataset-csv-<v>.zip`)**: All 7 CSV tables with markdown documentation.
- **Apache Parquet (`tar-dataset-parquet-<v>.zip`)**: Type-strict columnar files for zero-copy queries with DuckDB, Polars, and Arrow.
- **SQLite Database (`tar-dataset-sqlite-<v>.zip`)**: Pre-built relational database `tar.db` with indexed foreign keys.
- **AI Corpora (`tar-dataset-ai-<v>.zip`)**: JSONL fine-tuning, RAG knowledge corpus, and benchmark suite.
- **R Package (`theamazingrace_<v>.tar.gz`)**: CRAN-compliant source package for R (`library(theamazingrace)`).
- **Python Distribution (`.whl`, `.tar.gz`)**: Standalone `tar-dataset` CLI and schemas package.

## Quick Code Examples

### Querying Parquet with DuckDB (Python)
```python
import duckdb

# Compute top 5 teams by lowest racing average
duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT team_name, season, placement, racing_average
    FROM 'teams.parquet'
    WHERE winner = 1
    ORDER BY racing_average ASC
    LIMIT 5;
""").show()
```

### Loading in R via Companion Package
```r
# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("nicholaswilde/the-amazing-race/r")

library(theamazingrace)
library(dplyr)

data(teams)
data(leg_results)

# Analyze winner trajectory
winner_legs <- leg_results %>%
  inner_join(teams, by = "team_id") %>%
  filter(winner == 1)
```

### Querying SQLite Database
```bash
sqlite3 tar.db "SELECT season, winner, destination_summary FROM seasons LIMIT 5;"
```

### CLI Tool
```bash
# Inspect a season or team
tar-dataset inspect season 1
tar-dataset inspect team "Rob & Amber"

# Validate data integrity and schema
tar-dataset validate
tar-dataset stats
```
